transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Honestly, HR and my sister have both been saying I’ve gotten too thin. I don’t really see it that way—I just think my suits fit sharper. But my weight has kept dropping since the divorce, so they wanted me to come in.
Have you been intentionally trying to lose weight or cut back on what you eat?

Yeah. Most days it’s just coffee in the morning, maybe a protein bar between sales calls, then something small at night—like grilled chicken without rice. If I eat a full meal, it feels like I’ve messed up the whole day.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?
Yeah. If the scale is even a pound up after a client dinner or a weekend in Miami, I panic a little. It feels like I’m losing control, and I start figuring out how to cut back the next day.
Could you tell me your current height and weight?
I don’t have an exact number with me. I just know it’s kept dropping since the divorce. HR and my sister say I’m too thin, but I mostly notice my suits fitting sharper.
Have you noticed any decrease in your sex drive or sexual interest recently?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really paid much attention to that lately.
Have you noticed any difficulties with getting or maintaining an erection?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed or thought about that recently.
Roughly how much weight have you lost since the divorce?
I don’t know the exact amount. I just know it’s been steadily dropping since the divorce. My sister and HR think I’m too thin, though I mostly just notice my suits fitting sharper.
Do you push yourself to exercise intensely or excessively to burn calories and keep your weight down?
No, not really. It’s more that I keep my eating pretty limited—coffee in the morning, maybe a protein bar, then something small at night. If I eat a full meal, it feels like I’ve ruined the day.
When you look in the mirror, do you see parts of your body as being too fat or carrying excess weight?
Yeah. Before a meeting or a date, I’ll look at my stomach and my face and just focus on whether I look soft. If I do, I feel like people are going to see me as sloppy or weak.
Have you ever made yourself throw up after eating to keep from gaining weight?
No. I haven’t done that.
Have you used laxatives to help control or lose weight?
I’m not sure what you mean by laxatives.
Have you used any diet pills or medications to help suppress your appetite?
I don’t really know what counts as diet pills or appetite medications.
Have you ever taken water pills or diuretics to help you lose weight?
I’m not really sure what water pills or diuretics are.
Have you noticed that you feel unusually cold or have trouble staying warm when others are comfortable?
I haven’t really noticed that, no.
Have you experienced any dizziness, lightheadedness, or feeling like you might pass out when you stand up?
I’m not sure—I haven’t really noticed that happening.
Has a doctor or healthcare professional told you that your weight is dangerously low or that you are clinically underweight?
No doctor has told me that exactly. HR and my sister keep saying I’ve gotten too thin, but I just notice my suits fit sharper. My weight’s been dropping since the divorce.
Despite the weight you have lost, is your weight currently in the normal range for your height?
I don’t know if it’s considered normal. My weight has kept going down since the divorce, but I mostly just notice my suits fitting sharper. HR and my sister are the ones saying I’m too thin.
Have you taken any pills, teas, or remedies to force bowel movements or empty your bowels to help control your weight?
No, I haven’t taken anything like that.
Have you taken any pills, powders, or supplements to reduce your appetite or keep yourself from feeling hungry?
I’m not sure what would count as those. I haven’t noticed taking anything specifically to stop myself from feeling hungry.
Have you taken any pills or medications to make you urinate more frequently in order to shed water or lose weight?
No, I haven’t taken anything to make myself urinate more or lose water weight.
